newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London little changed, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London little changed, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady on Tuesday following Wall Street's record finish overnight as European investors waited to see if the Dow's meteoric rise would be sustained in the short-term, dealers said.

"Common sense would dictate that we should see some profit-taking on Wall Street today," one dealer said. "But trying to predict the Dow's movement on a day to day basis is becoming a difficult exercise."
On Monday, the Dow Industrials Average soared 143.29 points to a record closing level of 7,214.49 while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 33.91 points or 2.6 percent to 1,339.24.

Philip Morris Cos Inc which climbed $3-7/8 or nearly 10 percent on Monday after a favourable U.S. court ruling, was down $1/4 to $43-3/4 while RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp eased $1/8 to $32-1/2 after a $3 jump overnight.
Tobaccos soared on Monday after a Florida court ruled that R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco, was not negligent in the death of a former smoker.
Elsewhere, Intel Corp slipped $1/4 to $162-1/4 following a $4-7/8 advance on Monday while Digital Equipment Corp added $1/8 to $31-3/4.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was down 0.70 to 836.00 while the June T-bond eased 2/32 to 109-31/32 by 1025 GMT.
